stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan has faded, but its rain now threatens eastern India
stories.question: Where is Cyclone Akvan heading, and who in eastern India is at risk?
stories.dek: Akvan is no longer a cyclone. It weakened into a low-pressure area over Odisha on 20 November, but its leftover rain has put north Odisha, Bengal and Bihar at risk.

so_far.text: Akvan is a storm that moved in from the sea towards India's east coast. Iran proposed its name. Forecasters first projected it to hit Andhra Pradesh, but it shifted course towards Odisha. It was the third storm to threaten Odisha in 24 days. The Odisha government evacuated over 3 lakh people, set up 9,341 cyclone shelters and deployed 423 rescue teams. Several districts shut schools and colleges for two to three days, and Odisha banned fishing.

what_happened.text: Akvan began its landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha at around 8 am on 20 November 2026. Landfall is when a storm's centre crosses the coast. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) expected landfall to take about three hours, with winds of 70–90 km/h for six hours. Akvan had already weakened to a cyclonic storm on 19 November. On 20 November it degraded into a low-pressure area over central Odisha. On 21 November the IMD put Mayurbhanj and Balasore on red alert for heavy rain. It also forecast heavy rain for Bengal and Bihar. Kolkata was waterlogged.

steps.text: A cyclone runs on heat and moisture drawn from the warm sea water beneath it.
On 20 November Akvan's centre crossed the coast near Gopalpur, cutting off that supply of fuel.
Without fuel, and slowed by friction over land, it weakened into a low-pressure area over central Odisha.
But the weak system still held huge amounts of moisture, which kept falling as heavy rain.
So the risk shifted from coastal wind to rain and waterlogging in north Odisha, Bengal and Bihar.

history.text:
The root of this story is 29 October 1999. A super cyclone struck Odisha between Puri and Kendrapara, with winds near 260 km/h. About 10,000 people died. That disaster reshaped how the state manages disasters.

The test came on 12 October 2013. Cyclone Phailin made landfall near Gopalpur in Ganjam, the same stretch of coast as Akvan. After mass evacuations, 45 deaths were reported, far fewer than in 1999. Moving people early had worked.

On 3 May 2019, Cyclone Fani hit Puri. It was the strongest tropical cyclone to hit Odisha since 1999. On 20 May 2020, Super Cyclone Amphan made landfall near Bakkhali in West Bengal and affected about 44 lakh people. Bengal and Odisha have faced repeated Bay of Bengal storms since.

In November 2026, Akvan became the third storm to threaten Odisha in 24 days. It was first projected to hit Andhra Pradesh, then shifted course. Odisha used its familiar plan: evacuate over 3 lakh people and open 9,341 shelters. On 20 November Akvan crossed the coast near Gopalpur and weakened the same day. By 21 November, the danger had become heavy rain in north Odisha, Bengal and Bihar.

analogy.text: Think of a water tanker whose engine is failing. It slows down because it has lost its power, just as a cyclone loses wind once the warm sea is gone. But its tank is still full, and it leaks water wherever it rolls.
analogy.breaks: A storm has no driver or sealed tank. Winds high above steer it, and it can pick up some moisture over land.

for_you.text: If you live in or are travelling to Mayurbhanj or Balasore, expect heavy rain under a red alert. Thirteen more Odisha districts, including Cuttack, Puri and Khordha, are on orange alert. Kolkata is waterlogged, and Bengal and Bihar expect heavy rain. Check your train first: 69 were cancelled. It is not yet known when schools reopen or the fishing ban ends.

lesson.concept: Why a cyclone fades over land but its rain continues
lesson.big_idea: A cyclone gets its power from warm sea water. Once it crosses onto land, that fuel is cut and its winds fade. But the moisture it carries keeps falling as rain, often far inland.

steps.title: The sea is the fuel
steps.text: Warm sea water evaporates into the air above it. As that moist air rises and turns back into cloud droplets, it releases heat. That heat drives the rising air and the spinning winds of a cyclone.

steps.title: Landfall cuts the fuel
steps.text: Landfall is when the storm's centre crosses the coast. Akvan did this near Gopalpur on 20 November, with winds of 70–90 km/h. Over land there is no warm sea below, and rough ground slows the winds.

steps.title: It weakens in stages
steps.text: Storms drop down the scale in stages. Akvan had already weakened to a cyclonic storm on 19 November, a day before landfall. After crossing the coast on 20 November, it degraded into a low-pressure area over central Odisha: a weak swirl, far gentler than a cyclone.

steps.title: The water is still up there
steps.text: Weaker winds do not empty the clouds. The leftover system still holds huge amounts of water vapour. It drifts inland and drops that water as heavy rain, over places the strong wind never reached.

steps.title: The risk changes shape
steps.text: So the danger moves from wind on the coast to floods and waterlogging inland. That is why the IMD's red alerts on 21 November were for heavy rain.

example.setup: Imagine a storm that crosses the coast with winds of 90 km/h, then moves over a district of 1,000 square kilometres. All the numbers here are assumed, to keep it simple.

lines.label: Winds at landfall
lines.note: Akvan's winds at landfall were 70–90 km/h.

lines.label: Twelve hours inland
lines.note: Assume it loses 20 km/h every six hours without sea fuel.

lines.label: Rain on 1 sq km
lines.calc: Assume 100 mm on 1 sq km = 1 lakh tonnes
lines.note: 0.1 metre deep over 10 lakh square metres of land.

lines.label: Whole district
lines.calc: 1 lakh tonnes × 1,000 sq km = 10 crore tonnes
lines.note: All that water must drain away through rivers and drains.

example.result: The winds fell by almost half, so the storm looks much weaker. Yet the district still receives about 10 crore tonnes of water. That is why the danger moves from wind to rain.

apply.text: This is what happened with Akvan. Its winds were 70–90 km/h as it crossed the coast near Gopalpur on 20 November, and it faded to a low-pressure area the same day. But its moisture kept moving. So on 21 November the IMD put Mayurbhanj and Balasore on red alert for heavy rain, and Kolkata was waterlogged.

practice.q: Suppose the same weakened storm drops 50 mm of rain on a smaller district of 500 square kilometres. How much water falls?
practice.answer: First, one square kilometre: 50 mm is 0.05 metre, and 0.05 × 10 lakh square metres = 50,000 tonnes. Then the district: 50,000 × 500 = 2.5 crore tonnes. Half the rain on half the area gives a quarter of the water.

check.q: Akvan has weakened into a low-pressure area. Why are Mayurbhanj and Balasore still on red alert?
options: The storm is regaining cyclone strength over land
The weakened system still carries moisture that falls as heavy rain
Red alerts stay in place automatically for a month after any cyclone
check.why: Weakening cuts the wind, not the moisture. The leftover system still carries water vapour, which falls as heavy rain inland.

takeaways: Cyclones run on warm sea water; over land they weaken, but their rain keeps falling.
Akvan faded over Odisha on 20 November, yet its rain put north Odisha, Bengal and Bihar at risk.
Watch IMD district alerts and railway updates; alert end dates and damage figures are not yet known.

scenes.say: Cyclone Akvan 20 November ko India ke east coast par pahuncha. Toh ab yeh ja kahan raha hai, aur eastern India mein kise abhi bhi khatra hai? Short answer: cyclone chala gaya, lekin khatra nahi gaya.
scenes.speak: Cyclone Akvan 20 November को India के east coast पर पहुँचा। तो अब यह जा कहाँ रहा है, और eastern India में किसे अभी भी खतरा है? Short answer: cyclone चला गया, लेकिन खतरा नहीं गया।

scenes.say: Pehle dekhiye kya hua. 20 November ko subah lagbhag 8 baje, Akvan ne Odisha mein Gopalpur ke paas coast cross karna shuru kiya. Ise landfall kehte hain. India Meteorological Department, yaani IMD, ne kaha ki hawa 70 se 90 kilometre per hour ki thi, aur 6 ghante tak itni hi tez rahegi.
scenes.speak: पहले देखिए क्या हुआ। 20 November को सुबह लगभग 8 बजे, Akvan ने Odisha में Gopalpur के पास coast cross करना शुरू किया। इसे landfall कहते हैं। India Meteorological Department, यानी IMD, ने कहा कि हवा 70 से 90 kilometre per hour की थी, और 6 घंटे तक इतनी ही तेज़ रहेगी।

scenes.say: Phir yeh kamzor pad gaya. 19 November ko hi Akvan ghat kar cyclonic storm ban chuka tha. 20 November ko yeh central Odisha ke upar ek low-pressure area ban gaya. Matlab hawa ka ek halka sa ghumav, cyclone se kahin zyada narm. Toh Akvan ab koi cyclone nahi hai jo kahin ja raha ho.
scenes.speak: फिर यह कमज़ोर पड़ गया। 19 November को ही Akvan घट कर cyclonic storm बन चुका था। 20 November को यह central Odisha के ऊपर एक low-pressure area बन गया। मतलब हवा का एक हल्का सा घुमाव, cyclone से कहीं ज़्यादा नरम। तो Akvan अब कोई cyclone नहीं है जो कहीं जा रहा हो।

scenes.say: Lekin iski baarish aage badhti rahi. 21 November ko IMD ne north Odisha ke Mayurbhanj aur Balasore ko heavy rain ke liye red alert par rakha, jo uski sabse badi warning hai. Odisha ke 13 aur districts ko orange alert mila, yaani taiyaar rahiye. Bengal aur Bihar mein bhi heavy rain ka forecast tha, aur Kolkata mein paani bhar gaya.
scenes.speak: लेकिन इसकी बारिश आगे बढ़ती रही। 21 November को IMD ने north Odisha के Mayurbhanj और Balasore को heavy rain के लिए red alert पर रखा, जो उसकी सबसे बड़ी warning है। Odisha के 13 और districts को orange alert मिला, यानी तैयार रहिए। Bengal और Bihar में भी heavy rain का forecast था, और Kolkata में पानी भर गया।

scenes.speak: Odisha इतनी तेज़ी से काम क्यों करता है? चलिए 29 October 1999 पर चलते हैं। Puri और Kendrapara के बीच एक super cyclone आया, हवा लगभग 260 kilometre per hour। करीब 10 हज़ार लोग मारे गए। उस तबाही ने बदल दिया कि state disasters को कैसे संभालता है।

scenes.say: Asli test aaya 12 October 2013 ko. Cyclone Phailin Gopalpur ke paas pahuncha, coast ka wahi hissa jahan Akvan aaya. Bade paimaane par evacuation ke baad 45 maut report hui, 1999 se kahin kam. Logon ko jaldi hataana kaam kar gaya.

scenes.show: Warm sea = fuel. Land cuts it.
scenes.speak: तो cyclone कमज़ोर क्यों हुआ, लेकिन बारिश क्यों नहीं रुकी? पहली बात, cyclone अपने नीचे के गरम समुंदर के पानी से heat और moisture लेता है। दूसरी बात, जब Akvan ने Gopalpur के पास coast cross किया, तो यह supply कट गई।

scenes.say: Teesri baat, fuel ke bina, aur zameen par friction se dheema hokar, yeh low-pressure area ban gaya. Chauthi baat, iske andar ab bhi bahut saari moisture thi. Paanchvi baat, isliye khatra coast ki hawa se hatkar north Odisha, Bengal aur Bihar mein heavy rain ka ho gaya.
scenes.speak: तीसरी बात, fuel के बिना, और ज़मीन पर friction से धीमा होकर, यह low-pressure area बन गया। चौथी बात, इसके अंदर अब भी बहुत सारी moisture थी। पाँचवी बात, इसलिए खतरा coast की हवा से हटकर north Odisha, Bengal और Bihar में heavy rain का हो गया।

scenes.say: Ab players ki baat. IMD storm ko track karta hai aur alerts jaari karta hai. Odisha government ne evacuation aur shelters sambhale, aur 423 rescue teams lagayi. Do railway zones, East Coast Railway aur South Eastern Railway, ne trains cancel ki.
scenes.speak: अब players की बात। IMD storm को track करता है और alerts जारी करता है। Odisha government ने evacuation और shelters संभाले, और 423 rescue teams लगाईं। दो railway zones, East Coast Railway और South Eastern Railway, ने trains cancel कीं।

scenes.speak: अब numbers देखिए। Odisha में 3 लाख से ज़्यादा लोगों को evacuate किया गया। 1999 को याद कीजिए, जब करीब 10 हज़ार लोग मारे गए, और 2013 में Phailin को, जब mass evacuation से मौत सिर्फ़ 45 रही। अकेले Bhadrak district में 26 हज़ार से ज़्यादा लोगों को हटाया गया।

scenes.say: Ab woh ek idea jo seekhna hai. Cyclone ko taakat garam samundar ke paani se milti hai. Jaise hi yeh zameen par aata hai, woh fuel kat jata hai aur hawa kamzor padne lagti hai. Lekin jo moisture yeh saath laata hai, woh baarish banke girti rehti hai, aksar coast se kaafi andar tak.
scenes.show: Wind fades over land; rain doesn't
scenes.speak: अब वह एक idea जो सीखना है। Cyclone को ताकत गरम समुंदर के पानी से मिलती है। जैसे ही यह ज़मीन पर आता है, वह fuel कट जाता है और हवा कमज़ोर पड़ने लगती है। लेकिन जो moisture यह साथ लाता है, वह बारिश बनके गिरती रहती है, अक्सर coast से काफ़ी अंदर तक।

scenes.say: Step by step samjhiye. Garam samundar ka paani bhaap banta hai. Jab nami wali hawa upar uthkar baadal banati hai, toh heat chhodti hai, aur wahi heat ghoomti hawaon ko chalati hai. Landfall par garam samundar nahi rehta, aur ubad khabad zameen hawa ko dheema kar deti hai. Storms stages mein scale par neeche aate hain. Akvan landfall se ek din pehle hi kamzor ho chuka tha, aur coast cross karne ke baad low-pressure area ban gaya.
scenes.speak: Step by step समझिए। गरम समुंदर का पानी भाप बनता है। जब नमी वाली हवा ऊपर उठकर बादल बनाती है, तो heat छोड़ती है, और वही heat घूमती हवाओं को चलाती है। Landfall पर गरम समुंदर नहीं रहता, और ऊबड़ खाबड़ ज़मीन हवा को धीमा कर देती है। Storms stages में scale पर नीचे आते हैं। Akvan landfall से एक दिन पहले ही कमज़ोर हो चुका था, और coast cross करने के बाद low-pressure area बन गया।

scenes.say: Lekin kamzor hawa se baadal khaali nahi hote. Paani ki bhaap andar ki taraf jaati hai aur heavy rain banke girti hai. Storm का कोई driver नहीं होता, उसे ऊपर की हवाएँ चलाती हैं।

scenes.speak: चलिए कुछ made-up numbers लेते हैं। मान लीजिए एक storm 90 kilometre per hour पर coast cross करता है। और ज़मीन पर हर 6 घंटे में यह 20 खो देता है। 12 घंटे बाद, 90 minus 20 minus 20, बचे 50। हवा लगभग आधी हो गई।

scenes.say: Ek aam galti yeh sochna hai ki Akvan ab bhi ek cyclone hai jo eastern India paar kar raha hai. Aisa nahi hai. Ab asli baat baarish hai. stories.headline: Suspected methanol liquor kills 16 in Manipur's Chandel district
stories.question: How did spurious liquor kill so many in Manipur, and who is responsible?
stories.dek: Cheap liquor bought in Sugnu appears to have contained methanol, a poison you cannot taste. Sixteen are dead, hundreds were treated, and who is responsible is not yet established.

so_far.text: Spurious liquor is illegally made drink sold as real alcohol. In September 2026 a methanol liquor outbreak in Nagaland's Tuensang and Mokokchung districts killed at least 23 people. A special investigation team there is checking supply links to Assam. In Manipur, cases began around Wednesday 18 November in Chandel district, mainly in Chakpikarong. Police say the liquor was bought in Sugnu, in Kakching district. Patients came in with dizziness and stomach pain. Some needed haemodialysis, where a machine cleans the blood. On 20 November Chief Minister Y. Khemchand Singh visited hospitals in Imphal.

what_happened.text: As of 1 pm on 21 November, a Chandel district health official put the death toll at 16. Shija Hospitals in Imphal alone treated over 346 patients. BABINA and JNIMS hospitals each took about 60. The Anal Naga Union says over 600 were admitted by 20 November, so the true total is unclear. Medical findings shared with the union indicate 70–80% of cases were methanol poisoning; lab tests are awaited. Chandel police say the liquor was bought in Sugnu, not made in Chandel. Kakching Police and food safety officials seized locally brewed liquor from seven Sugnu locations. Reports differ on whether two or six people were arrested.

steps.text: Real liquor contains ethanol. Methanol is a cheap industrial alcohol that looks, smells and tastes almost the same.
Illegal brewers face no testing, so methanol can enter a batch, added for strength or left by careless distilling.
Police say this liquor was bought in Sugnu, Kakching, and drunk in Chandel villages such as Chakpikarong. Who made it is unknown.
The body turns methanol into poison slowly, so symptoms appear hours later, after many people have already drunk.
Patients went mostly to Imphal hospitals, some needing dialysis. The Anal Naga Union wants better healthcare in Chandel itself.

history.text: Deaths from illegal liquor are not new in India. The root problem is the same each time: drink made outside the law, with no one testing what is in it. Nagaland has banned alcohol under its Total Prohibition Act since 1989. Yet illegal liquor still reaches drinkers there, and groups want the law reviewed. Manipur has its own record. In July 2017 five people died after drinking spurious liquor. Police detained Abu Kamei and his mother as alleged suppliers. In 2019 a raid in Thoubal reportedly broke up a factory making fake IMFL (Indian-made foreign liquor, meaning branded bottled spirits) after deaths. It showed that illegal supply in Manipur has a long history. In Gujarat, which also bans alcohol, a Deccan Herald report counted 156 hooch (illegal liquor) deaths in 2019 and 46 in 2022. Bans did not end the trade. In June 2024 methanol liquor killed about 65 people in Kallakurichi, Tamil Nadu. That state then raised penalties to life imprisonment and a fine of at least ₹10 lakh when bootlegging causes deaths. In September 2026 a methanol outbreak in Nagaland killed at least 23 people. About two months later came the deaths in Chandel, from liquor that police say was bought in Sugnu.

analogy.text: Think of a counterfeit medicine strip. It looks like the real thing, but one wrong ingredient makes it dangerous, and you cannot tell by looking. Methanol is that wrong ingredient: in the glass, it passes for ethanol.
analogy.breaks: A fake pill usually just fails to work. Methanol actively turns into a poison inside your body, hours after you drink it.

for_you.text: Wherever you live in India, the practical lesson is the same. Methanol cannot be seen, smelled or tasted, so only sealed, licensed liquor is safe. Dizziness, stomach pain or blurred vision hours after drinking is an emergency. Early hospital care, including dialysis, saves lives. In Manipur, families are still waiting for confirmed ex-gratia payments.

misconception.myth: Banning alcohol stops deaths from illegal liquor.

check.q: Why did many victims seem fine at first and fall ill only later?
options: The liver slowly turns methanol into a toxic acid, so harm shows hours later
Methanol is weaker than ethanol, so it takes longer to feel drunk
Spurious liquor becomes poisonous only after it is stored for days
check.why: The liver converts methanol step by step into formic acid. That acid, which builds up over hours, does the damage.

Kuch ko haemodialysis ki zaroorat padi, jismein ek machine khoon saaf karti hai. 20 November ko Chief Minister ne Imphal ke hospitals ka daura kiya.

scenes.speak: अब हाल की घटनाएँ। Cases लगभग Wednesday, 18 November से Chandel district में शुरू हुए, ख़ास कर Chakpikarong में। मरीज़ों को चक्कर और पेट दर्द था। कुछ को haemodialysis की ज़रूरत पड़ी, जिसमें एक machine ख़ून साफ़ करती है। 20 November को Chief Minister ने Imphal के hospitals का दौरा किया।

scenes.say: Toh aisa hua kyun? Asli sharab mein ethanol hota hai. Methanol ek sasta industrial alcohol hai, jo dikhne, soonghne aur swaad mein lagbhag same lagta hai. Illegal banane walon ki koi testing nahi hoti, isliye methanol mil sakta hai. Ya toh strength ke liye milaya jaata hai, ya laaparwah distilling se reh jaata hai.
scenes.show: Ethanol or methanol? You can't tell
scenes.speak: तो ऐसा हुआ क्यों? असली शराब में ethanol होता है। Methanol एक सस्ता industrial alcohol है, जो दिखने, सूँघने और स्वाद में लगभग same लगता है। Illegal बनाने वालों की कोई testing नहीं होती, इसलिए methanol मिल सकता है। या तो strength के लिए मिलाया जाता है, या लापरवाह distilling से रह जाता है।

scenes.say: Police kehti hai ki yeh sharab Sugnu mein kharidi gayi aur Chandel ke gaon mein pi gayi. Kisne banayi, yeh abhi pata nahi. Body methanol ko dheere dheere zeher mein badalti hai, isliye symptoms ghanton baad aaye, jab bahut log pee chuke the. Zyadatar mareez Imphal ke hospitals gaye, kuch ko dialysis chahiye tha. Anal Naga Union chahti hai ki Chandel mein hi behtar healthcare ho.
scenes.speak: Police कहती है कि यह शराब Sugnu में ख़रीदी गई और Chandel के गाँवों में पी गई। किसने बनाई, यह अभी पता नहीं। Body methanol को धीरे धीरे ज़हर में बदलती है, इसलिए symptoms घंटों बाद आए, जब बहुत लोग पी चुके थे। ज़्यादातर मरीज़ Imphal के hospitals गए, कुछ को dialysis चाहिए था। Anal Naga Union चाहती है कि Chandel में ही बेहतर healthcare हो।

scenes.say: Ab players kaun hain? Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh ne enquiry aur doshiyon ko saza ka vaada kiya hai, aur Chandel mein ek specialist medical team bheji. Anal Naga Union special investigation team aur compensation maang rahi hai. Kakching Police ne sharab zabt ki. Sabse zyada mareezon ka ilaaj Shija Hospitals ne kiya.
scenes.speak: अब players कौन हैं? Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh ने enquiry और दोषियों को सज़ा का वादा किया है, और Chandel में एक specialist medical team भेजी। Anal Naga Union special investigation team और compensation माँग रही है। Kakching Police ने शराब ज़ब्त की। सबसे ज़्यादा मरीज़ों का इलाज Shija Hospitals ने किया।

scenes.say: Is story ke peeche ek idea hai: methanol body mein zeher kaise banta hai. Ek nakli dawai sochiye, jo asli dikhti hai lekin usmein ek galat ingredient chhupa hai. Methanol bhi asli alcohol jaisa lagta hai. Lekin nakli goli ke ulat, yeh aapke andar formic acid ban jaata hai, ek zeher jo ghanton tak badhta hai aur andha kar sakta hai ya jaan le sakta hai.
scenes.speak: इस story के पीछे एक idea है: methanol body में ज़हर कैसे बनता है। एक नकली दवाई सोचिए, जो असली दिखती है लेकिन उसमें एक ग़लत ingredient छुपा है। Methanol भी असली alcohol जैसा लगता है। लेकिन नकली गोली के उलट, यह आपके अंदर formic acid बन जाता है, एक ज़हर जो घंटों तक बढ़ता है और अंधा कर सकता है या जान ले सकता है।

scenes.say: Step by step samjhiye. Liver wahi enzyme use karta hai jo woh ethanol par karta hai. Woh methanol ko pehle formaldehyde banata hai, phir formic acid. Yeh acid optic nerve par hamla karta hai, jo aankh ko dimaag se jodne wala cable hai, aur khoon ko acidic bana deta hai. Ismein ghante lagte hain, isliye peene wala shuru mein normal mehsoos karta hai.
scenes.speak: Step by step समझिए। Liver वही enzyme use करता है जो वो ethanol पर करता है। वो methanol को पहले formaldehyde बनाता है, फिर formic acid। यह acid optic nerve पर हमला करता है, जो आँख को दिमाग़ से जोड़ने वाला cable है, और ख़ून को acidic बना देता है। इसमें घंटे लगते हैं, इसलिए पीने वाला शुरू में normal महसूस करता है।

scenes.say: Lagbhag 12 se 24 ghante baad chakkar, pet dard aur dhundhla dikhna shuru hota hai. Doctor do tarah se ladte hain. Ek dawai, ya aam ethanol bhi, liver ko busy rakhti hai, taaki kam acid bane. Aur haemodialysis khoon se methanol aur acid ko filter kar deta hai.
scenes.show: Block the liver, clean the blood
scenes.speak: लगभग 12 से 24 घंटे बाद चक्कर, पेट दर्द और धुंधला दिखना शुरू होता है। Doctor दो तरह से लड़ते हैं। एक दवाई, या आम ethanol भी, liver को busy रखती है, ताकि कम acid बने। और haemodialysis ख़ून से methanol और acid को filter कर देता है।

stories.headline: India crosses one crore HPV vaccine doses in under nine months
stories.question: India has given one crore HPV vaccine doses: what does that mean for cervical cancer?
stories.dek: Most of the girls targeted in 2026 now have the vaccine against the virus behind most cervical cancer. The payoff, fewer cancers and deaths, will only show up years from now.

so_far.text: On 28 February 2026, India launched a free national HPV vaccination campaign for girls aged 14, about 1.15 crore girls a year. Each girl gets one dose of the Gardasil-4 vaccine, and parental consent is voluntary. Girls turning 15 within 90 days of the launch could also get it. By 11 September 2026, 80 lakh doses had been given. Progress was uneven. Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram had reached 100% of their targets, and Uttar Pradesh alone had vaccinated over 22 lakh girls. Chhattisgarh, Sikkim, Kerala, Telangana and Odisha had crossed only 60%. Parental consent was a key barrier in places such as Delhi.

what_happened.text: On 21 November 2026, the Union Health Ministry said India had crossed 1 crore HPV vaccine doses in under nine months of the national campaign. The ministry says about 87% of target girls have been covered. Each girl needs only one dose, so the number of doses is roughly the number of girls vaccinated. The total rose from 80 lakh on 11 September 2026. That is about 20 lakh more doses in roughly ten weeks. The latest state-by-state breakdown available is from September.

steps.text: Long-lasting HPV infection causes cervical cancer. In India, types 16 and 18 cause about 70% of cases.
A vaccine given before exposure stops those infections. An AIIMS expert says it cuts pre-cancer and cancer risk by about 90–95%.
India gives one free dose of Gardasil-4 at age 14. Each year's group is about 1.15 crore girls.
One crore doses in under nine months means about 87% of target girls have now been vaccinated.
But untreated pre-cancer takes 10–15 years to become cancer, so fewer cases will only show up over the long term.

history.text:
India first tried HPV vaccination in 2008, in limited pilot projects. No national rollout followed. Safety concerns, misinformation and logistics held it back for years.

In 2016, Punjab and Sikkim launched limited programmes of their own. These were state programmes, not a national one.

Later, the Union Budget announced HPV vaccination for girls aged 9 to 14. The government then narrowed the target to 14-year-olds. That decision took nearly two years and was informed by NTAGI, the government's expert advisers on vaccines.

In November 2024, ICMR, India's main medical research body, began studying how 500 girls aged 9 to 14 respond to a single dose.

The national campaign began on 28 February 2026, giving one dose of Gardasil-4 bought through Gavi. By 11 September, 80 lakh doses had been given. On 21 November, the total crossed 1 crore.

lesson.concept: How a vaccine at 14 prevents cancer years later
lesson.big_idea: The HPV vaccine stops the infection behind most cervical cancer before it starts. Because this cancer grows slowly, a dose given at 14 prevents cases that would have appeared ten or more years later.

steps.title: HPV is a common infection
steps.text: HPV, the human papillomavirus, spreads through sexual contact. Most infections clear on their own. A few last for years and damage cells of the cervix, the lower part of the womb.

steps.title: Cancer grows slowly
steps.text: A lasting infection creates pre-cancer lesions, which are patches of abnormal cells. If untreated, they take 10–15 years to become cancer. That long gap is why results take time.

steps.title: A few types do most harm
steps.text: Some HPV types are far more dangerous than others. In India, just two, types 16 and 18, cause about 70% of cervical cancer cases. So blocking the worst types prevents most of the risk.

steps.title: Vaccinate before exposure
steps.text: The vaccine trains the body to block the virus. It cannot clear an infection that is already there, so it is given early, at 14. An AIIMS expert says this cuts pre-cancer and cancer risk by about 90–95%.

steps.title: Coverage sets the total
steps.text: The share of girls vaccinated decides how many future cancers are avoided. The health ministry says about 87% of target girls have been covered.

apply.text: So when the ministry reports 1 crore doses and about 87% coverage, most of the 2026 group of 14-year-old girls are like the 8,700 vaccinated girls in our town. If the AIIMS expert's estimate holds, most of the cancers they would have faced will not happen. But India's 1,20,000 yearly cases will not drop soon. That fall comes over the long term.

practice.q: Same town, but coverage is only 60%, like the slowest states in September. How many of the 100 future cancers are left?
practice.answer: Girls vaccinated: 60% of 10,000 = 6,000. Their future cases: 60% of 100 = 60. Prevented: 90% of 60 = 54. Left: 100 − 54 = 46. That is about twice the 22 left at 87% coverage.

stories.headline: AI sell-off drags gold and Bitcoin down as India draws buyers
stories.question: Why are AI stocks, Bitcoin and gold all falling, while India holds up?
stories.dek: Doubts about AI profits pushed US stocks into a correction, and investors sold gold and Bitcoin too. Foreign money is moving into India, which investors see as a market with little AI exposure.

so_far.text: Since 2025, investors have argued over whether the AI boom is a bubble. By late 2025, five companies made up about 30% of the S&P 500, the main US index of 500 large companies. In 2026 the doubts started to cause real damage. In July, Oracle's credit rating was cut, and South Korea's Kospi index began a crash of about 44% in 40 days. On 19 November, Anthropic listed its shares at $83 each, raising about $81bn. The same day, the S&P 500 fell 2%.

what_happened.text: On Friday 20 November the US sell-off got worse. The Nasdaq, a tech-heavy index, erased all its 2026 gains. The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones entered a correction, meaning a fall of over 10% from their peak. The S&P 500 had its worst week since April 2025. Nvidia fell 6.9% by midday despite strong earnings. ABC News reported that Anthropic closed down 10.8% at $86.72, still above its $83 listing price. Other outlets report different figures. Bitcoin fell below $60,000, its lowest in over two years, then bounced about 9% on 21 November. Gold and silver had their worst week in eight months.

steps.text: Investors doubt that AI spending will earn enough revenue, so they will pay less for AI shares.
New worries piled on: midterm results favouring data-centre curbs, a US chip-loophole closure, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation.
A few AI giants make up a big share of US indexes, so their fall dragged the S&P 500 and Dow into correction.
Gold fell too, under pressure from a strong dollar, bets on Fed rate rises and selling tied to the AI sell-off.
Some foreign money moved into India, seen as a 'non-AI trade', bringing record buying in November.

history.text: The story starts in January 2025. China's DeepSeek released an AI model that matched costlier rivals. Nvidia, the AI chip maker, lost about 17% of its value, about $600bn, in one day. That raised a question: will huge spending on AI pay off? Spending kept growing anyway. The Stargate venture planned $500bn of AI infrastructure. In July 2025 Nvidia became the first $4tn company, and in October 2025 it passed $5tn. Its $100bn investment in OpenAI drew criticism as circular financing, where partners fund each other's purchases. The Bank of England and the IMF warned of a sharp correction. By late 2025, five companies made up about 30% of the S&P 500, the highest concentration in roughly half a century. This meant a fall in a few AI firms could now drag down the whole market. In 2026 the doubts started to cause real damage. In March, OpenAI dropped plans to expand its flagship Stargate data centre in Abilene, Texas. In May, the Financial Stability Board warned of risks in private credit, the loans from non-bank lenders that help fund the AI build-out. In July, S&P cut Oracle's rating to one notch above junk, and the Kospi began a crash of about 44% in 40 days. Gold and Bitcoin were sliding too. Gold hit a record $5,594.82 on 29 January 2026. By late June it was down about 29%, as bets on US rate rises weighed on it. Bitcoin hit a 21-month low of $57,737 in July.

lesson.concept: How a sell-off spreads, and where money goes
lesson.big_idea: When one big bet goes wrong, investors often sell other things too, even safe ones, to raise cash. Some cash then moves to markets that seem far from the fear.

steps.title: Investors hold baskets
steps.text: A big fund rarely owns one thing. It may hold tech shares, gold, crypto and foreign shares together. A loss in one part shrinks the whole basket.

steps.title: Losses bring demands for cash
steps.text: When the basket shrinks, lenders may ask for loans back, or nervous investors may ask for their money. Either way, the fund must sell something.

steps.title: Sell what you can
steps.text: A fund in a hurry sells what is easy to sell, like gold. Selling falling shares near the bottom locks in big losses. So safe assets fall too.

steps.title: Rates and the dollar add pressure
steps.text: Gold pays no interest. If the US Federal Reserve, the US central bank, may raise rates, bank deposits earn more, so gold looks worse. A strong dollar adds pressure.

steps.title: Money that stays seeks shelter
steps.text: Some money moves to markets seen as far from the fear. Geojit's V.K. Vijayakumar says foreigners now see India as a 'non-AI trade'.

scenes.say: Here is the idea to learn: how a sell-off spreads, and where the money goes. When one big bet goes wrong, investors often sell other things too, even safe ones, to raise cash. Some of that cash moves to markets that seem far from the fear.

Step one: big funds hold baskets of tech shares, gold, crypto and foreign shares. Step two: losses bring demands for cash, from lenders or nervous investors. Step three: you sell what you can, not what you want. Easy-to-sell assets like gold go first.

scenes.say: Step four: gold pays no interest. If rates are expected to rise, cash in the bank earns more, so gold looks less attractive. A strong dollar adds pressure. Step five: money that stays in shares looks for shelter. Geojit's Vijayakumar says foreigners now see India that way.

Let's try an example. Imagine a fund with one hundred crore rupees: sixty crore in AI stocks, twenty in gold, twenty in Bitcoin. AI stocks fall twenty per cent. Twenty per cent of sixty crore is twelve crore. So the fund is now worth eighty-eight crore.

Nervous investors want ten crore back. Selling AI stocks near the bottom locks in losses. So the fund sells five crore of gold and five crore of Bitcoin. That leaves seventy-eight crore. Now picture thousands of funds doing this. Gold falls, though nothing changed about gold.

What do analysts think? Capital Economics, a research firm, forecasts an AI bust in twenty twenty-seven. Geojit's Vijayakumar says the US sell-off triggered the shift into India. A State Street strategist says India needs steady earnings growth to justify its higher share prices.

stories.headline: Trump threatens penalties on US firms building data centres abroad
stories.question: Why does Trump want to punish US firms building data centres abroad?
stories.dek: Trump says data centres built abroad could fall to China, so he threatened a "tremendous tax". But no rate, rule or date exists yet, and it is unknown if India's AI hubs would be covered.

so_far.text: Data centres are large buildings full of computer chips that run cloud services and AI. US tech firms are building many of them abroad. In September 2026 Alphabet announced about $15bn for data centres in Finland. In India, Google plans a $15bn AI hub at Visakhapatnam, and Amazon Web Services has pledged $12.7bn. India is trying to attract more data centres with a 20-year tax holiday.

what_happened.text: On 20 November 2026, at a White House press conference, President Donald Trump threatened 'tremendous penalties' on US tech firms that build data centres outside the US. CNBC reported that he threatened a 'tremendous tax'. He said that if US firms build abroad, China will take the data centres. He gave no tax rate, enforcement agency, start date, executive order or bill. The Latin Times reported that taxing power lies with Congress and that Trump's staff reportedly were not briefed. Data-centre and tech shares fell the same day.

steps.text: AI runs on data centres: huge buildings of computer chips that need a lot of electricity.
Trump says the US leads the AI race and China is second: 'There really is no third place.'
He argues that if US firms build data centres in other countries, China will take them.
Trump gave no details, but any tax on building abroad would add to the cost of foreign sites.
Separately, adviser Peter Navarro objected in January 2026 to US data-centre power serving AI users in India and China.

history.text:
The story starts with a Biden-era rule, the 'AI diffusion framework'. It sorted countries into tiers, and India was in Tier 2. Firms in Tier 1 had to keep 75% of their AI computing power in Tier 1 nations. Industry said this complicated building AI abroad.

In January 2025 OpenAI, SoftBank and others announced Stargate, a $500bn vehicle for AI infrastructure in the US. In May 2025 Trump struck AI and chip deals with Gulf states. This raised fears in the US that chips could reach China. On 19 November 2025 the Commerce Department authorised advanced chip exports to Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN. So AI power was going abroad, but Washington was choosing where.

India became a big destination. In October 2025 Google announced a $15bn, 1 GW AI hub at Visakhapatnam, its biggest India investment. Amazon Web Services pledged $12.7bn. In 2025 some US firms also put India leases on hold for over two months during US-India trade tensions.

In January 2026 Trump adviser Peter Navarro asked why Americans were paying for AI in India. In February 2026 India offered a 20-year tax holiday for global data centres. In September 2026 Alphabet announced about $15bn for Finland. Then, on 20 November 2026, came Trump's threat.

lesson.concept: How a penalty changes where a firm builds
lesson.big_idea: A firm builds where the total cost is lowest. A penalty on building abroad adds cost to the foreign site, and it pulls the firm home only if it is bigger than the saving.

steps.title: Firms compare total costs
steps.text: A company choosing where to build a data centre adds up land, power, chips and staff at each site. It picks the cheaper site that still serves its customers.

steps.title: A penalty raises one side
steps.text: A penalty, such as a tax on building abroad, adds cost only to the foreign site. On 20 November 2026 Trump threatened a 'tremendous tax' of this kind.

steps.title: Compare again with the penalty
steps.text: Add the penalty to the foreign cost. If that total is higher than the home cost, home wins. If it is still lower, the firm keeps building abroad.

steps.title: Host countries push back
steps.text: Host countries can cut the foreign cost. India offered a 20-year tax holiday for global data centres in February 2026, so a penalty would need to be bigger to win.

steps.title: Only a real law bites
steps.text: A threat is not a tax. Taxing power lies with Congress. Until a bill or order sets a rate, firms can only guess the size of the penalty.

example.setup: Suppose a US firm can build a data centre abroad for $8bn, or at home for $10bn. Assume the penalty is 30% of what it spends abroad.

lines.label: Gap without penalty
lines.note: Abroad is $2bn cheaper, so the firm would build abroad.

lines.label: Penalty at 30%
lines.note: Added only to the foreign site.

lines.label: Real cost abroad
lines.note: Foreign build plus the penalty.

lines.label: Compare
lines.note: Home is now $0.4bn cheaper.

example.result: The penalty ($2.4bn) is bigger than the saving from building abroad ($2bn), so the firm switches home. A smaller penalty would not change its choice.

apply.text: Trump gave no rate, so firms cannot yet do this sum for real projects such as Google's $15bn Visakhapatnam hub or Alphabet's roughly $15bn Finland plan. India's 20-year tax holiday lowers the foreign cost, so any penalty would need to be bigger to pull such projects home.

practice.q: Same firm: $8bn abroad, $10bn at home. But now assume the penalty is 20%. Where does it build?
practice.answer: Penalty: 20% of $8bn = $1.6bn. Cost abroad: $8bn + $1.6bn = $9.6bn. That is less than $10bn at home. So it still builds abroad and saves $0.4bn.

check.q: If Trump's penalty became law, when would it actually push a firm to build at home?
options: When the foreign cost plus the penalty is higher than the home cost

check.why: A penalty changes the choice only if it is bigger than the money the firm saves by building abroad.

takeaways: A penalty moves a firm home only if it is bigger than the saving from building abroad.

stories.headline: Anthropic mathematician claims AI-aided proof of the Riemann hypothesis
stories.question: Has an AI-assisted mathematician really proved the Riemann hypothesis?
stories.dek: Not yet confirmed. A computer has checked the logic of Levent Alpöge's Claude-assisted proof. But a check that it states the right problem is still pending, and no human-readable version exists.

so_far.text: The Riemann hypothesis, proposed in 1859, is a claim about the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. That function encodes how prime numbers are spread out. Proving the hypothesis wins a US$1 million Clay Millennium Prize. By 2020, mathematicians had proved that about 41.6% of the zeros sit where the hypothesis says. In August 2026, Alpöge and Furman of Anthropic, the AI company, claimed over 67.25%. Anthropic said that technique would not prove the full hypothesis. On 19 November 2026, Anthropic made its stock-market debut.

what_happened.text: On 20 November 2026, Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, posted a four-page note on his website, alpo.ge. 'I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,' he wrote. He says the method also proves the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. The proof was released only as Lean code in 14 packages. Lean is a language in which a computer checks each logical step. The same day, MIT's Andrew Sutherland compiled the code independently. Hours later, Ravi Vakil, president of the American Mathematical Society, shared a rival all-human draft by Alessandro Masullo. Within about eight hours, problems were found in it.

steps.text: The proof is far too long for people to read; Alpöge says a human-readable version would exceed 250,000 pages.
So he released it as Lean code, where a computer accepts each step only if it follows logically.
Sutherland compiled that code independently, which is why he puts the chance of anything fishy at approximately zero.
But Lean only checks the statement as typed; if the hypothesis was mistranslated into code, the proof proves something else.
That 'comparator' check was still pending, and Alpöge admits he has not fully mastered the surrounding mathematics, so nothing is accepted yet.

history.text:
The story begins in 1859. In a paper on counting prime numbers, Riemann proposed that every non-trivial zero of the zeta function has real part 1/2. In plain words, all these zeros sit on one line, called the 'critical line'. This matters because the zeros control the error in the prime number theorem, which estimates how many primes there are. If the hypothesis is true, prime counts stray from their average by the smallest amount possible.

No one could prove it, so mathematicians proved parts of it. In 1914, Hardy showed that infinitely many zeros lie on the line, but not what share. In 1942, Selberg proved that a positive proportion does. Levinson raised that to one-third in 1974, and Conrey to two-fifths in 1989. Work in 2020 reached about 41.6%.

Meanwhile, many results were proved only by assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, a wider version. One was Miller's 1976 fast test for whether a number is prime. It became unconditional, meaning true without that assumption, only when the AKS test arrived in 2002.

In August 2026, Alpöge and Furman of Anthropic claimed over 67.25% of zeros lie on the line, a large jump. Anthropic said that method would not prove the whole hypothesis. Then, on 20 November 2026, Alpöge claimed the full proof.

It still matters as a test of how far to trust a proof that a computer has checked but no person yet fully understands.

lesson.concept: How a computer checks a proof, and its blind spot
lesson.big_idea: A proof checker like Lean confirms that every step of a proof follows logically. But it only checks the statement typed in, so someone must still confirm that statement is the real problem.

steps.title: A proof is a chain
steps.text: A proof starts from accepted facts and moves in small steps to the claim. Each step must follow from earlier ones. If one step breaks, the whole proof fails.

steps.title: Long proofs defeat human readers
steps.text: People check proofs by reading them, and errors hide in long ones. Alpöge says a human-readable version of his proof would exceed 250,000 pages, far more than anyone can check quickly.

steps.title: Lean checks every step
steps.text: In Lean, the statement and every step are written as code. The computer will not 'compile', or accept, the proof if any step fails to follow. Sutherland compiled Alpöge's code independently on 20 November.

steps.title: The blind spot: the statement
steps.text: Lean proves exactly what was typed. If the problem was mistranslated into code at the start, a perfect proof proves the wrong thing. A 'comparator' check, matching the code to the real hypothesis, was still pending.

steps.title: Then humans must understand it
steps.text: Even a checked proof needs people to understand and review it before the community accepts it. Alpöge plans a human-readable write-up in the coming months.

example.setup: Imagine you want Lean to prove a simple claim: 'every number in the list 2, 4, 6 is even'. You type the claim into Lean, but make a small typo.

lines.label: Claim in words
lines.note: What you actually want proved.

lines.label: Claim as typed
lines.note: Assume the typo dropped the 6.

lines.label: Lean checks proof
lines.note: Every step is valid, so the proof compiles.

lines.label: Comparator check
lines.note: Compares the typed claim with the real one.

lines.label: Fix and recheck
lines.note: Now the green light means what you meant.

example.result: Lean's green light was honest: the logic was right. But it proved a smaller claim than you wanted. Only the comparator check showed the typed statement was not the real one.

apply.text: So Sutherland's successful compile on 20 November shows the logic of Alpöge's Lean code holds. That is why he puts the chance of anything fishy at approximately zero. What remains is our 'comparator' line: checking that the code states the real Riemann hypothesis. That check was still pending, and no human-readable proof exists yet.

practice.q: Suppose a Lean proof compiles, but the typed statement only says 'at least two-thirds of the zeros lie on the critical line'. What has been proved?
practice.answer: Lean confirms the logic, so the typed claim is proved. But the Riemann hypothesis says every non-trivial zero is on the line. Two-thirds is not every zero. The comparator check would flag a mismatch: this is a partial result, like the August 2026 claim of over 67.25%, not the hypothesis.

check.q: Sutherland's Lean compile succeeded. What important question does it still leave open?
options: Whether the code states the real Riemann hypothesis

check.why: Lean already checks every logical step. It cannot tell whether the hypothesis was typed into code correctly; that is the pending comparator check.

takeaways: Lean checks every logical step, but only for the statement as typed into code.
Alpöge's Claude-assisted Riemann proof compiles in Lean but is not yet accepted or understood by people.
Watch for the comparator check and Alpöge's human-readable write-up, planned for the coming months.

history.text:
This story has two roots. The first is Yemen. In September 2014 the Houthis, a rebel movement, seized the capital Sanaa and toppled President Hadi's government. In March 2015 Saudi Arabia led a coalition into Yemen at Hadi's request, as the Houthis closed on Aden. A civil war became a regional one. In March 2022 the coalition said it would cease hostilities, and Oman hosted Houthi-Saudi talks. In 2023 Saudi Arabia and Iran restored diplomatic ties. But in October 2023 the Houthis began attacking Red Sea shipping.

The second root is Iran's nuclear programme. On 14 July 2015 Iran and world powers signed a nuclear deal, the JCPOA. In 2018 the US walked out and reimposed sanctions under "maximum pressure". In June 2025 Israel and the US struck Iran's nuclear facilities. Beforehand, the IAEA, the UN nuclear watchdog, estimated Iran held 440.9 kg of 60%-enriched uranium. How much survives is unclear. That stockpile is what Araqchi now calls a red line.

In early 2026 indirect US-Iran talks ran in Muscat and Geneva. On 28 February US-Israeli strikes began. In March Iran announced Hormuz closed. Then the two roots joined: in mid-July fighting in Yemen reignited, and on 20 July the Houthis declared a blockade of Saudi shipments.

lesson.big_idea: Enrichment is the share of uranium that is the useful U-235 type. Diluting mixes it with weaker uranium, so the share drops even though nothing leaves the country.

steps.title: What the percentage means
steps.text: Natural uranium is mostly a type called U-238. Only U-235 splits easily to release energy. 'Enriched to 60%' means 60 of every 100 kg is U-235. Before June 2025, the IAEA estimated Iran held 440.9 kg at 60%.

steps.title: Higher share, closer to a bomb
steps.text: Power reactors run on uranium with a low share of U-235. Weapons need a very high share, around 90%. So material at 60% has already covered most of the path.

steps.title: Mixing lowers the share
steps.text: Diluting means blending the 60% material with uranium that has almost no U-235. The amount of U-235 stays the same. But it is spread through more total material, so the percentage falls.

steps.title: Going back up is hard
steps.text: To use diluted uranium for a weapon, you must enrich it again in centrifuges, machines that spin uranium gas to separate U-235. That takes time and is hard to hide from inspectors.

steps.title: Why supervision matters here
steps.text: Iran says keeping its highly enriched uranium inside Iran is a red line. Diluting it under IAEA supervision has been floated: inspectors watch the mixing, so the material stays but loses its quick weapons value.

example.setup: Suppose a country holds 10 kg of uranium enriched to 60%. It agrees to dilute it with uranium that, assume, has almost no U-235.

lines.label: U-235 inside
lines.note: Only this part decides the percentage.

lines.label: Add blend uranium
lines.note: Assume the added 110 kg has about zero U-235.

lines.label: New share
lines.note: Same U-235, spread across twelve times more material.

lines.label: What changed
lines.note: Nothing left the country, but it needs re-enriching to be dangerous.

example.result: Dilution removes nothing. The same 6 kg of U-235 is spread through twelve times more material, so the share drops from 60% to 5%. Making it weapons fuel again would need fresh, visible enrichment.

apply.text: That is why dilution is the possible 'fair solution' Araqchi hinted at. His red line is that highly enriched uranium stays in Iran. Blending it down under IAEA supervision keeps it there while cutting its weapons value. But how much of the 440.9 kg survived June 2025 is unclear, and the report does not say which terms Trump rejects.

practice.q: Suppose a country holds 20 kg of uranium at 60%. How much near-zero uranium must it add to bring the share down to 4%?
practice.answer: U-235 inside: 60% of 20 kg = 12 kg. At 4%, those 12 kg must be 4% of the total, so total = 12 ÷ 0.04 = 300 kg. It already has 20 kg, so it adds 300 − 20 = 280 kg.

scenes.say: Hathiyar ke liye lagbhag 90 percent chahiye, toh 60 kaafi aage hai. Dilute karna matlab usmein aisa uranium milana jismein U 235 na ke barabar ho. U 235 ki matra wahi rehti hai. Lekin woh zyada material mein fail jaata hai, isliye percentage gir jaata hai.
scenes.speak: हथियार के लिए लगभग 90 percent चाहिए, तो 60 काफ़ी आगे है। Dilute करना मतलब उसमें ऐसा uranium मिलाना जिसमें U 235 न के बराबर हो। U 235 की मात्रा वही रहती है। लेकिन वो ज़्यादा material में फैल जाता है, इसलिए percentage गिर जाता है।

scenes.say: Ise phir se khatarnak banane ke liye centrifuges chahiye, yaani aisi machines jo uranium gas ghumakar U 235 alag karti hain. Yeh dheema kaam hai aur inspectors se chhupana mushkil. Isliye IAEA ki nigrani mein dilution se material Iran mein rehta hai, par uski jaldi hathiyar banane wali value khatam ho jaati hai.
scenes.speak: इसे फिर से खतरनाक बनाने के लिए centrifuges चाहिए, यानी ऐसी machines जो uranium gas घुमाकर U 235 अलग करती हैं। यह धीमा काम है और inspectors से छुपाना मुश्किल। इसलिए IAEA की निगरानी में dilution से material Iran में रहता है, पर उसकी जल्दी हथियार बनाने वाली value खत्म हो जाती है।

scenes.say: Chaliye karke dekhte hain. Maan lijiye ek desh ke paas 60 percent wala 10 kilogram hai. Yaani 6 kilogram U 235. Ab 110 kilogram milaiye, jismein maan lete hain U 235 lagbhag zero hai. Ab total hua 120. 6 ko 120 se bhaag dijiye. Mila 5 percent.
scenes.speak: चलिए करके देखते हैं। मान लीजिए एक देश के पास 60 percent वाला 10 kilogram है। यानी 6 kilogram U 235। अब 110 kilogram मिलाइए, जिसमें मान लेते हैं U 235 लगभग zero है। अब total हुआ 120। 6 को 120 से भाग दीजिए। मिला 5 percent।

stories.headline: COP31 runs into overtime as fossil fuels and finance split nations
stories.question: Why are the COP31 climate talks running late, and what is India actually objecting to?
stories.dek: A COP decision passes only if no country objects, so one holdout can stall a deal. Panama wants fossil-fuel commitments back. India's group rejects an electrification target in the main text.

so_far.text: COP31 is the 2026 UN climate summit, held in Antalya, Türkiye, under COP31 President Murat Kurum. Countries must agree its main political text, called the cover decision, by consensus. On 19 November a revised nine-page draft dropped all references to transitioning away from fossil fuels. It kept a goal for electricity to supply 35% of global final energy by 2035, and still mentioned keeping 1.5C within reach. The same day, Panama said it would object to any deal missing its eight conditions.

what_happened.text: As of 21 November 2026, COP31 was in overtime with no final deal. A late session on Friday, 20 November approved only technical matters, not the wider political deal. Two splits remain. Will the deal mention fossil fuels? Will it address money to help poorer countries adapt to climate change? More than a dozen countries, including Panama, demanded a clear transition away from fossil fuels. EU Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said it will be "either a good deal or no deal". COP31 President Murat Kurum said: "We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet."

steps.text: COP decisions need consensus, so one country's formal objection can stop the main deal.
The 19 November draft removed fossil-fuel language, leaving softer goals like 35% electrification by 2035 and 1.5C.
More than a dozen countries, including Panama, demand a clear fossil-fuel transition; Panama says it will object without it.
India and its group object to the electrification target in the negotiated text, calling it top-down and unfunded.
The draft also dropped the $120bn-a-year adaptation figure, so finance demands stay unmet and no text yet satisfies everyone.

history.text: The story starts in 1992, when countries signed the UN climate convention, the UNFCCC, at the Rio Earth Summit. They have met every year since at a COP, short for Conference of the Parties, except in 2020. In 1997 the Kyoto summit set emissions targets for rich countries. Since then, decisions by consensus have shaped how the talks work: no country can simply be outvoted. In 2015, at COP21, all countries adopted the Paris Agreement. It set a stretch goal of limiting warming to 1.5C, and every country adopted it, not just rich ones. In 2023, COP28 in Dubai became the first COP accord to name fossil fuels. Countries rejected 'phase-out' and 'phase-down' wording and settled on 'transitioning away'. COP30 later had a roadmap for that transition. On 19 November 2026, the revised COP31 draft dropped both the COP28 wording and the COP30 roadmap. Because every country must agree, that edit became one of the main fights keeping the talks in overtime.

lesson.concept: How consensus lets one country stall a COP deal
lesson.big_idea: At a COP, a decision passes only when no country formally objects. So the text shrinks to what everyone accepts, and any single country can hold out.

steps.title: What consensus means
steps.text: Consensus is not a vote. The chair asks whether anyone objects. If no one does, the gavel falls and the decision passes. Since the 1997 Kyoto summit, consensus has shaped how COPs work.

steps.title: Every objection forces an edit
steps.text: If a group objects to a line, the chair usually rewrites or removes it. The Like-Minded Developing Countries, including India, object to the electrification target sitting in the cover decision.

steps.title: Edits can create new objectors
steps.text: Removing a line can upset those who wanted it. The 19 November draft dropped fossil-fuel transition language; Panama now says it will object to any deal missing its conditions, such as an oil production cap.

steps.title: When nothing fits, talks overrun
steps.text: If no wording satisfies everyone, the deadline passes and talks go into overtime. Panama wants majority voting when consensus fails, which would remove the single-country veto.

example.setup: Imagine 100 countries (assume this number) agreeing one text by consensus. Line A is a fossil-fuel promise; 10 countries oppose it. Line B is an electrification target; a different 10 oppose it.

lines.label: Majority vote, Line A
lines.note: Under voting, the 90 would win easily.

lines.label: Consensus, Line A
lines.note: Any objection must be met by removing or rewriting.

lines.label: Consensus, Line B
lines.calc: Another 10 object: Line B is cut
lines.note: Same rule, different objectors.

lines.label: Text left
lines.calc: Neither line remains: a weak text
lines.note: Now countries who wanted Line A may object.

lines.label: One objector
lines.note: Under consensus, even one objection stops adoption.

example.result: Under consensus, every line someone dislikes gets cut, and the shrinking text can then lose its own supporters. Even 1 objector in 100 can stop a deal that a majority vote would pass easily.

apply.text: That is COP31 now. The 19 November draft cut fossil-fuel language, like Line A. India's group wants the electrification target, like Line B, out of the cover decision. Panama says it will object to a text without fossil-fuel commitments. With no wording everyone accepts, talks were still in overtime on 21 November.

practice.q: Suppose the same 100 countries consider Panama's idea of majority voting. 70 support it and 30 oppose. Does it pass by majority vote? By consensus?
practice.answer: Majority vote: 70 is more than half of 100, so it passes. Consensus: 30 countries object, and one objection is enough, so it fails. Under a consensus rule, even the switch to voting can be blocked.

steps.text: Nepal is landlocked between India and China, so its trade and travel must cross a neighbour's land or sky.
That makes routes the core of the relationship: roads, power links and flight paths, which is why connectivity and energy lead the reported agenda.
When a route is disrupted, as in the 2015–16 blockade, ties suffer and the distrust lasts for years.
Lipulekh adds a question of ownership: India and China plan trade through a pass that Nepal claims as its own.
So the reported agenda covers trade, energy and connectivity, while an unresolved border question sits in the background.

history.text:
The story starts with trust. In 2015–16 a blockade on the India–Nepal border strained ties, and the Kathmandu Post still lists it as a sore point. Later, under the previous Oli government, Nepal's constitutional map showed Kalapani, Limpiyadhura and Lipulekh as Nepali. That put the border claim into Nepal's constitution itself.

Then Nepal's leadership changed. Shah took office on 27 March 2026, and Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said Modi invited him right after. By April 2026 there was a new irritant. India and China had announced they would reopen trade through Lipulekh without consulting Kathmandu. A Kathmandu Post editorial urged a commitment to consult Nepal on any future Lipulekh trade. In May 2026 Nepal reportedly sent diplomatic notes to India and China, restating its claim to all three areas.

In early June 2026 Rabi Lamichhane, chairman of the RSP party, met Modi, Jaishankar and Doval in Delhi. The Kathmandu Post read that as a signal of a reset. Shah's visit on 22–23 November 2026, his first to India as prime minister, comes after that signal.

lesson.concept: Why a landlocked country lives by its routes
lesson.big_idea: A landlocked country has no coast, so almost everything it trades must cross a neighbour's land or sky. The more routes it has, the less any one closure can hurt it.

steps.title: No coast means borrowed doors
steps.text: A landlocked country has no seaport of its own. Ships cannot reach it, so goods arrive by road, rail, power line or plane across a neighbour. Nepal sits between India and China.

steps.title: Each route is a door
steps.text: Think of every border road, power line and flight path as a door. Each door has a capacity: how many trucks, units of power or flights it can carry each day.

steps.title: Few doors mean high exposure
steps.text: If one door carries most of the traffic and it shuts, supplies fall short fast. The Kathmandu Post lists the 2015–16 blockade as a lasting sore point in India–Nepal ties.

steps.title: A full door also hurts
steps.text: A door can be open but crowded. In April 2026 the Kathmandu Post named an extra air route for Nepal as a possible deliverable, because current routes are congested.

steps.title: Who owns the doorway matters
steps.text: Routes can cross disputed land. Nepal claims Lipulekh, yet India and China announced reopening trade through it without consulting Kathmandu.

example.setup: Imagine a hill town that needs 80 truckloads of goods a day. Two roads lead in, and each road can carry 50 trucks a day.

lines.label: Total capacity
lines.note: More than the 80 needed, so shelves stay full.

lines.label: Road A shuts
lines.note: Only one door is left.

lines.label: Shortfall
lines.note: Goods the town cannot get.

lines.label: Share missing
lines.note: More than a third of daily needs gone.

lines.label: Add Road C
lines.note: With a third door, one closure no longer causes a shortage.

example.result: With two doors, losing one cuts supplies by more than a third. A third door covers the gap. That is why the number and width of routes matter so much to a landlocked country.

apply.text: So reports put trade, connectivity and energy on Shah's agenda, and each is a door in our example. The extra air route the Kathmandu Post floated in April 2026 would add a door beside crowded ones. The 2015–16 blockade showed what one shut door costs. And Lipulekh is a doorway Nepal says is its own.

practice.q: The same town now needs 90 trucks a day. It has three roads carrying 40 trucks each. One road shuts. How short is the town?
practice.answer: Capacity before: 40 + 40 + 40 = 120 trucks. One road shuts: 120 − 40 = 80 trucks. Shortfall: 90 − 80 = 10 trucks a day. Share missing: 10 ÷ 90 is about 11%. More doors, smaller shock.

scenes.speak: तो routes और एक pass इतने ज़रूरी क्यों हैं? पहली बात, Nepal landlocked है, India और China के बीच। उसका trade और सफ़र किसी पड़ोसी की ज़मीन या आसमान से होकर ही गुज़रता है। इसलिए reported agenda में connectivity और energy सबसे आगे हैं।

scenes.say: Doosri baat, jab koi route band hota hai, jaise blockade mein hua, toh rishte bigadte hain aur avishwas saalon tak rehta hai. Teesri baat, Lipulekh malikana haq ka sawaal jodta hai. India aur China us pass se trade ki planning kar rahe hain jis par Nepal daava karta hai. Matlab agenda mein trade aur routes hain, aur background mein ek border ka sawaal baitha hai.
scenes.speak: दूसरी बात, जब कोई route बंद होता है, जैसे blockade में हुआ, तो रिश्ते बिगड़ते हैं और अविश्वास सालों तक रहता है। तीसरी बात, Lipulekh मालिकाना हक़ का सवाल जोड़ता है। India और China उस pass से trade की planning कर रहे हैं जिस पर Nepal दावा करता है। मतलब agenda में trade और routes हैं, और background में एक border का सवाल बैठा है।

scenes.say: Ab players. Balendra Shah, March se Nepal ke prime minister. Prime Minister Modi, jinhone unhe invite kiya aur jo unse mil rahe hain. Shisir Khanal, Nepal ke foreign minister, jinhone bataya ki invitation Shah ke office lete hi aa gaya tha. Aur Rabi Lamichhane, jinki June wali Delhi meetings ko reset maana gaya.
scenes.speak: अब players। Balendra Shah, March से Nepal के prime minister। Prime Minister Modi, जिन्होंने उन्हें invite किया और जो उनसे मिल रहे हैं। Shisir Khanal, Nepal के foreign minister, जिन्होंने बताया कि invitation Shah के office लेते ही आ गया था। और Rabi Lamichhane, जिनकी June वाली Delhi meetings को reset माना गया।

scenes.say: 2 numbers yaad rakhiye. 3: woh ilaake jo Nepal ka constitutional map Nepali dikhata hai, Kalapani, Limpiyadhura aur Lipulekh. Aur 2: is visit ke din, jo prime minister ke roop mein Shah ka pehla India visit hai.
scenes.speak: 2 numbers याद रखिए। 3: वो इलाके जो Nepal का constitutional map Nepali दिखाता है, Kalapani, Limpiyadhura और Lipulekh। और 2: इस visit के दिन, जो prime minister के रूप में Shah का पहला India visit है।

scenes.say: Ab woh idea jisse yeh kahani samajh aati hai: ek landlocked desh apne routes ke sahare kyun jeeta hai. Landlocked desh ke paas samundar ka kinara nahi hota. Woh jo bhi trade karta hai, lagbhag sab kuch kisi padosi ki zameen ya aasmaan se guzarta hai. Jitne zyada routes, kisi ek ke band hone se utna kam nuksaan.
scenes.speak: अब वो idea जिससे ये कहानी समझ आती है: एक landlocked देश अपने routes के सहारे क्यों जीता है। Landlocked देश के पास समुंदर का किनारा नहीं होता। वो जो भी trade करता है, लगभग सब कुछ किसी पड़ोसी की ज़मीन या आसमान से गुज़रता है। जितने ज़्यादा routes, किसी एक के बंद होने से उतना कम नुकसान।

scenes.say: Chaliye step by step samjhte hain. Pehla: coast nahi, matlab darwaze udhaar ke. Doosra: har sadak, har power line aur har flight path ek darwaza hai, jiski ek capacity hai. Teesra: agar ek bada darwaza band ho jaye, toh supplies jaldi kam pad jaati hain.
scenes.speak: चलिए step by step समझते हैं। पहला: coast नहीं, मतलब दरवाज़े उधार के। दूसरा: हर सड़क, हर power line और हर flight path एक दरवाज़ा है, जिसकी एक capacity है। तीसरा: अगर एक बड़ा दरवाज़ा बंद हो जाए, तो supplies जल्दी कम पड़ जाती हैं।

scenes.say: Chautha: darwaza khula ho sakta hai lekin bhara hua, jaise Nepal ke congested air routes. Paanchva: darwaze ka maalik kaun hai, yeh bhi matter karta hai. Nepal Lipulekh par daava karta hai, phir bhi India aur China ne Nepal se poochhe bina uske raaste trade ka elaan kar diya.
scenes.speak: चौथा: दरवाज़ा खुला हो सकता है लेकिन भरा हुआ, जैसे Nepal के congested air routes। पाँचवाँ: दरवाज़े का मालिक कौन है, ये भी matter करता है। Nepal Lipulekh पर दावा करता है, फिर भी India और China ने Nepal से पूछे बिना उसके रास्ते trade का ऐलान कर दिया।

scenes.say: Ek example se samjhiye. Maan lijiye ek pahadi shehar ko roz 80 truck maal chahiye. Wahan 2 sadkein jaati hain, har ek par 50 truck. Dono milakar 100 truck, zaroorat se zyada. Ab sadak A band ho gayi. Sirf 50 truck andar aa paate hain.
scenes.speak: एक example से समझिए। मान लीजिए एक पहाड़ी शहर को रोज़ 80 truck माल चाहिए। वहाँ 2 सड़कें जाती हैं, हर एक पर 50 truck। दोनों मिलाकर 100 truck, ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा। अब सड़क A बंद हो गई। सिर्फ़ 50 truck अंदर आ पाते हैं।

scenes.say: Shehar ko chahiye 80, mil rahe hain 50. Yaani roz 30 truck kam, ya zaroorat ka saadhe saintees percent. Ab ek teesri sadak jodiye jo 30 truck laati hai. 50 plus 30, ho gaye 80. Kami khatam. Zyada darwaze, chhota jhatka.
scenes.show: A third door covers the gap
scenes.speak: शहर को चाहिए 80, मिल रहे हैं 50। यानी रोज़ 30 truck कम, या ज़रूरत का साढ़े सैंतीस percent। अब एक तीसरी सड़क जोड़िए जो 30 truck लाती है। 50 plus 30, हो गए 80। कमी ख़त्म। ज़्यादा दरवाज़े, छोटा झटका।

scenes.say: Ab wapas news par. Shah ke reported agenda mein trade, connectivity aur energy hain. Hamare example mein inmein se har ek ek darwaza hai. April mein Kathmandu Post ne ek extra air route ka idea diya tha, yaani bheed wale darwazon ke bagal mein ek naya darwaza. Blockade ne dikhaya ki ek band darwaze ki keemat kya hoti hai. Aur Lipulekh woh darwaza hai jise Nepal apna kehta hai.
scenes.speak: अब वापस news पर। Shah के reported agenda में trade, connectivity और energy हैं। हमारे example में इनमें से हर एक एक दरवाज़ा है। April में Kathmandu Post ने एक extra air route का idea दिया था, यानी भीड़ वाले दरवाज़ों के बगल में एक नया दरवाज़ा। Blockade ने दिखाया कि एक बंद दरवाज़े की क़ीमत क्या होती है। और Lipulekh वो दरवाज़ा है जिसे Nepal अपना कहता है।

scenes.say: Toh India mein aapke liye iska kya matlab hai? Zyadatar logon ke liye seedha asar chhota hai jab tak deals sign nahi hote, aur ab tak koi confirm nahi hai. Nazar rakhiye trade aur energy deals par, air route wale idea par, aur Lipulekh par, jahan China ke saath India ka planned trade route us zameen se guzarta hai jis par Nepal daava karta hai.
scenes.show: Small effect until deals are signed
scenes.speak: तो India में आपके लिए इसका क्या मतलब है? ज़्यादातर लोगों के लिए सीधा असर छोटा है जब तक deals sign नहीं होते, और अब तक कोई confirm नहीं है। नज़र रखिए trade और energy deals पर, air route वाले idea पर, और Lipulekh पर, जहाँ China के साथ India का planned trade route उस ज़मीन से गुज़रता है जिस पर Nepal दावा करता है।

scenes.say: Ek correction. Aap padh sakte hain ki Shah ne pledge kiya hai ki woh India ko China ke khilaf nahi khelenge. Unhone aisa nahi kiya. Yeh line Kathmandu Post ke ek editorial se aayi, jo unhe aisa pledge karne ki salah de raha tha. Yeh paper ki salah hai, unka vaada nahi.
scenes.speak: एक correction। आप पढ़ सकते हैं कि Shah ने pledge किया है कि वो India को China के ख़िलाफ़ नहीं खेलेंगे। उन्होंने ऐसा नहीं किया। ये line Kathmandu Post के एक editorial से आई, जो उन्हें ऐसा pledge करने की सलाह दे रहा था। ये paper की सलाह है, उनका वादा नहीं।

scenes.say: Aage kya dekhna hai? Modi ke saath baatcheet 23 November 2026 ko hone ki ummeed hai. Dekhiye ki trade, energy ya technology par deals sign hote hain ya nahi, aur air route par koi baat aati hai ya nahi. Jo ab tak pata nahi: kaun se agreements sign honge, agar koi hua toh, aur kya Lipulekh ya Kalapani formally agenda par hain.
scenes.speak: आगे क्या देखना है? Modi के साथ बातचीत 23 November 2026 को होने की उम्मीद है। देखिए कि trade, energy या technology पर deals sign होते हैं या नहीं, और air route पर कोई बात आती है या नहीं। जो अब तक पता नहीं: कौन से agreements sign होंगे, अगर कोई हुआ तो, और क्या Lipulekh या Kalapani formally agenda पर हैं।

scenes.say: 3 baatein yaad rakhiye. Landlocked desh apne routes ke sahare jeeta hai, aur zyada routes ka matlab hai ek ke band hone par kam nuksaan. Nepal ke naye prime minister 22 aur 23 November ko India mein hain, aur reported agenda par trade, energy aur connectivity hai. Aur 23 November ki baatcheet mein nazar rakhiye signed deals par aur Lipulekh par kisi bhi baat par.
scenes.speak: 3 बातें याद रखिए। Landlocked देश अपने routes के सहारे जीता है, और ज़्यादा routes का मतलब है एक के बंद होने पर कम नुकसान। Nepal के नए prime minister 22 और 23 November को India में हैं, और reported agenda पर trade, energy और connectivity है। और 23 November की बातचीत में नज़र रखिए signed deals पर और Lipulekh पर किसी भी बात पर।

quiz.q: Akvan has weakened into a low-pressure area. Why are Mayurbhanj and Balasore still on red alert?
options: The storm is regaining cyclone strength over land
The weakened system still carries moisture that falls as heavy rain
Red alerts stay in place automatically for a month after any cyclone
quiz.why: Weakening cuts the wind, not the moisture. The leftover system still carries water vapour, which falls as heavy rain inland.

quiz.q: Why did many victims seem fine at first and fall ill only later?
options: The liver slowly turns methanol into a toxic acid, so harm shows hours later
Methanol is weaker than ethanol, so it takes longer to feel drunk
Spurious liquor becomes poisonous only after it is stored for days
quiz.why: The liver converts methanol step by step into formic acid. That acid, which builds up over hours, does the damage.

quiz.q: Why won't India's cervical cancer cases fall sharply right after the one crore milestone?
options: The vaccine needs a second dose before it starts working
Pre-cancer takes 10–15 years to become cancer, so the gains show later
Only four states have vaccinated any girls so far
quiz.why: The vaccine stops infections in 14-year-olds now. The cancers it prevents would only have appeared after years of slow pre-cancer growth.
